name: progress
description: A horizontal progress bar for communicating operation completion percentage or indeterminate loading state. Built on Radix UI Progress. Tracks with a fill indicator driven by value 0–100 or null for indeterminate.

intent.Loading: Determinate progress — value is 0–99. Fill bar represents percentage complete.
intent.Complete: value=100. Fill bar spans full track width.
intent.Indeterminate: value=null or undefined. No measurable percentage — use CSS animation on indicator.

SM.when: Compact contexts — inline with text, table cells, tight layouts.

LG.when: Prominent status — onboarding steps, upload progress, large feature areas.

fill.note: Fill radius must match container radius to avoid clipping artefacts.

value.range: 0 to max for determinate; null for indeterminate

behavior.stateTransitions: Loading→Complete: set value to 100. Loading→Indeterminate: set value to null. Figma State dimension is for design documentation only — code is entirely value-driven.
behavior.widthMechanism: Radix sets --radix-progress-indicator-transform CSS property. Shadcn uses transform:translateX() on the indicator — fill spans 100% of track, position-shifted to simulate partial width.
behavior.indeterminateAnimation: Radix does not include an indeterminate animation by default. Target [data-state='indeterminate'] on root or [data-radix-progress-indicator] with a CSS keyframe.
behavior.indeterminateCss: @keyframes progress-indeterminate { 0% { transform: translateX(-100%); } 50% { transform: translateX(0%); } 100% { transform: translateX(100%); } }

accessibility.role: progressbar (set by Radix on root element)
accessibility.keyboard: Progress bars are not interactive — no keyboard interaction.
accessibility.indeterminateLabel: aria-valuetext omitted; provide surrounding context text for screen readers.

accessibility.contextText: Always pair with a visible label naming what is progressing — 'Uploading…', 'Processing files', 'Step 2 of 5'.

constraints: Always pair with a visible label naming what is progressing.
Use State=Indeterminate (value=null) for operations with no measurable percentage — never fake progress with slow-advancing determinate.
Show State=Complete as a final state before unmounting — give users a moment to register success.
Do not use progress for page load spinners — use a spinner or skeleton instead.
Leave State=Complete visible briefly before unmounting — 500–1000ms delay is appropriate.
Do not override the fill color from a parent — change className on <Progress> or extend the token.

useCases: Showing file upload completion percentage as a user uploads a document or image
Tracking multi-step onboarding — 'Step 2 of 5' with the bar showing 40% complete
Displaying a profile completeness score ('Your profile is 70% complete')
Showing a storage quota usage bar in account settings ('2.1 GB of 5 GB used')
Indicating that a background server-side job is running when no percentage is available (Indeterminate)
Confirming an import or export has finished by transitioning to State=Complete before unmounting

State=Loading.whenToUse: Determinate progress — a known percentage that updates as the operation advances

State=Complete.whenToUse: Operation has finished — show briefly before unmounting to confirm success

State=Indeterminate.whenToUse: Operation is running but no percentage can be computed

Size=SM.whenToUse: Compact contexts where the bar is a supporting detail
examples: Inline with a label in a dense layout

Size=MD.whenToUse: General use — cards, panels, settings pages

Size=LG.whenToUse: Prominent status — onboarding, large feature areas, hero progress
examples: Upload progress in a full-panel uploader

comparedTo.situation: Loading duration is unknown and no percentage can be shown
comparedTo.notInstead: progress State=Indeterminate (use indeterminate only when an active operation is clearly running)

comparedTo.situation: A single binary action (save, submit) needs a loading indicator
comparedTo.notInstead: progress (progress implies measurable advancement, not a momentary action)

comparedTo.situation: Content is loading on initial page load and the structure should be visible
comparedTo.notInstead: progress (skeleton preserves layout; progress does not)

notes: Figma State/Size variants are for design documentation only — in code everything is driven by value prop and className for height.

darkMode.notes: No known dark mode differences — all tokens are semantic and mode-aware.
